clue.text: National leader veers off racecourse

indicators.note: the leading letter of the racecourse's name turns away and is lost

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A horse veers off the course at a race meeting, led astray at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like a description of a race (the Grand National) but is the definition. ASCOT, an English racecourse, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Remarkable Belgians performing, not live

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters acting out a new routine, so they are rearranged
not tells us that the letters for live are excluded from the mix

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Some Belgians give a remarkable performance, though it is not live.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: rearranging BELGIANS gives the answer plus BE ('live'), so 'not' takes BE away and 'performing' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or notable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Abroad, a thousand separately enter coast, a part of peninsula

indicators.note: enter means going inside the coast word, here the second piece's turn
separately says the two incoming pieces do not go in side by side but each at its own spot

parts.note: a coast is a shore
abroad means out, away from home
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A thousand people abroad land at different points on a peninsula's coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' matters: the two pieces split up, one after the first letter of the coast word and one after its second, giving SOUTHKORE before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: South Korea occupies the southern half of the Korean peninsula.

clue.text: Vehicle engine cover half made of such steel?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: half asks for only the front portion of the word for the engine cover

parts.note: the bonnet is the British word for a car's engine cover (the hood in the US)

explanation.surface: A car whose bonnet is partly made of some kind of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: The bonnet is the British name for what Americans call the hood; 'half' keeps its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon steel is a common grade of steel, so the answer names that kind of steel.

clue.text: Gall as old Greek character almost drowned in beer

indicators.note: something drowned in beer is submerged within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is not reached

parts.note: kappa is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An old Greek character has the gall to drown his sorrows in beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gall' reads as cheek but is the plant growth. 'Almost' drops the final A of the Greek letter, leaving KAPP.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round growth on an oak tree caused by a wasp, a kind of plant gall.

clue.text: Green shade clothing brothers

definitions.meaning: ... green is a shade of green
... Bros is a British menswear and suit-hire business, so the ... brothers deal in clothing

explanation.surface: A green shade worn by some brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss is a muted green colour, and Moss Bros is a long-established British firm hiring out formal clothes.

clue.text: Period of which the present day is near the end

definitions.text: Period of which the present day is near the end

parts.words: Period of which the present day is near the end
parts.note: the present day is not today but Christmas Day, the day for presents, which falls late in this month

explanation.surface: A period of history whose final stretch is roughly now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present day' seems to mean the modern age; it is the day of presents, the 25th.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Day, 25th, falls six days before the close of this last month of the year.

clue.text: Woman's rotten idea scaled down

indicators.note: scaled down means reduced in size, so only a small portion of these words is kept

explanation.surface: A woman's bad plan gets trimmed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits inside rottEN IDea; 'Woman's' is 'Woman is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, as in the author Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Some potato? A lot ordered with a snack in the tube

parts.note: a chip is a bit of potato

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new arrangement, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone orders a lot of chips with a snack while on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is the sausage skin. 'Ordered' turns A LOT into OLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, a bite-sized snack inside its casing.

clue.text: Theatre is nothing to heartless devil

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is cut out

parts.note: a demon is a devil

explanation.surface: A theatre means nothing to a cruel devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes out the central M, leaving DEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a British cinema chain, and the word itself comes from the Greek name for a theatre for music.

clue.text: International computer system's not hard, in my opinion

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: the Net, short for the internet, is the worldwide computer network
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the worldwide network is not difficult to use.
explanation.walkthrough: THE NET (the internet) drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief that someone holds, a firm opinion.

clue.text: Spooner and Imogen agree where Doll Tearsheet worked

definitions.text: Spooner and Imogen agree where Doll Tearsheet worked

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: Doll Tearsheet is a prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2, so she is found at a whores' place
a prostitute works in bed

explanation.surface: The setter and Spooner find common ground over where a Shakespearean character plied her trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings fit: Doll worked at the Boar's Head tavern in Eastcheap, and, as a prostitute, in a whore's bed, which Spooner turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boar's Head was the Eastcheap tavern in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays where Falstaff drank and Doll Tearsheet plied her trade.

clue.text: Mac to use moisturiser

definitions.meaning: a mac is a waterproof raincoat, short for mackintosh
to apply oil to one's skin, read as two words

explanation.surface: A man called Mac is told to use moisturiser.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof coat of oiled cloth, and split as oil skin it means applying cream to the face.

clue.text: Cunning creature tucks head down a minute: it brings relief

indicators.note: the creature's first letter is moved down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: the fox is proverbially cunning

explanation.surface: A wily fox curls up with its head lowered for a moment's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: FOX with its F moved to the end gives OXF, then A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a charity providing famine and disaster aid around the world.

clue.text: All our letters after B: A goes, for a start

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar

indicators.note: for a start means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A line about learning the alphabet, moving from B to A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After B' reads like an alphabet lesson; here 'after' is POST, followed by B, A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the full collection of letters a person or office receives.

clue.text: See the end of Harry Potter prepared for printing plate

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement
the end of means the final letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at the final pages of a Harry Potter book ready for print.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE, the Y from the end of Harry, and POTTER are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype was a solid metal plate cast from a mould of set type, used for printing.

clue.text: Interrupting wind energy for resident temporarily

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a gust is a burst of wind
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A burst of wind energy disturbs someone staying for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside GUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest stays in a house or hotel for a limited time, a short-term resident.

clue.text: Female, inwardly modest, showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: inwardly means only the inside of the word is used, the outer letters dropped

parts.note: demure means modest and shy

explanation.surface: A modest woman shows just a glimpse of her leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of leg' sounds racy but is a bone. 'Inwardly' strips the outer D and E, leaving EMUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, part of the leg's skeleton.

clue.text: About to tuck into brownish-red biscuit

indicators.note: to tuck into means to go inside the other word

parts.note: maroon is a brownish-red colour
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to eat a reddish-brown biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' suggests eating, but it is the insertion signal; ca. (circa) is the usual abbreviation for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a sweet almond or coconut biscuit.

clue.text: Go just over five days?

indicators.note: just over a portion of the week, so the end is clipped off

parts.note: a working week is five days long

explanation.surface: A question about taking a trip of a little more than five days.
explanation.walkthrough: Three-quarters of WEEK, losing its K, is a fair stand-in for five-sevenths, a bit over five days. 'Go' is a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: To go, in informal use, is to urinate, which is to have a wee.

clue.text: New moon was spotted eventually by outdoor worker

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged
eventually means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A new moon was finally seen by someone working out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: MOON, WAS and D, the last letter of spotted, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman works in forests, felling and tending trees.

clue.text: Whiskey wanted back that is in inaccessible place

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: Someone wants their whiskey returned and it's stashed somewhere out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is reversed and IE added.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest, built high on a crag, so a remote lofty spot.

clue.text: It was used for building the holy city? Wrong

parts.note: Mecca is Islam's holy city
no is the reply to a wrong guess

explanation.surface: A query whether a toy set built the holy city, quickly dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks 'Mecca?' and answers 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a construction toy of metal strips, nuts and bolts for making models.

clue.text: Writing on page about excuse

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed after the other in the answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
text is writing

explanation.surface: Writing on a page about an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' means coming after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one.

clue.text: They may subsidise part of service, but only with one rupee

indicators.note: only with one means keeping a single copy of the letter, so one of the pair is dropped

parts.note: prayers form part of a church service
R is the abbreviation for rupee

explanation.surface: Someone may fund part of a service as long as it costs a rupee.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAYERS has two Rs; one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who pay contribute money, so payers may fund or subsidise something.

clue.text: In affection, bind daughter in embrace, finally close

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken
in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: near means close

explanation.surface: A tender scene of a parent hugging a daughter close.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the end of 'embrace', comes before NEAR with D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone loved, binding them by affection.

clue.text: I rouse fools with cunning, no joking

indicators.note: fools, as a verb, means tricks, hinting the letters are jumbled

parts.note: sly means cunning

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of stirring fools with their cunning, and means it.
explanation.walkthrough: I ROUSE rearranged gives SERIOU, then SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriously, said earnestly, signals that one is in earnest and not jesting.

clue.text: Swimmer to show off briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: to swank is to show off

explanation.surface: A swimmer who likes to show off for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANK, British slang for showing off, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a bird that swims on lakes and rivers.

clue.text: Miscellaneous stuff ends with these

parts.note: the phrase for assorted bits is the ends and these, paired together

explanation.surface: A remark on how a jumble of things finishes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends with these' seems to mean finishes; it means the word 'ends' goes with these in the stock phrase odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends is an idiom for assorted leftover items.

clue.text: All the Spanish make commotions

explanation.surface: All the Spanish people kick up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Todos is the Spanish word for everyone, and to-dos are fusses or rows.

clue.text: Origin of privileged performer

definitions.meaning: the source from which something grows
a ... in a tennis tournament is a ranked player given a favourable draw

explanation.surface: The origins of a privileged performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed means a source of growth, and a top-ranked player kept apart in a draw.

clue.text: Miss a film that wins Oscar

indicators.note: a film that wins something takes it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Skip a film that wins an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award; it is O in the radio alphabet, going inside VID after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to steer clear of it, to miss it deliberately.

clue.text: People carrier's small opening to reverse in a narrow street

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the other words

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street

indicators.note: to reverse means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A people carrier has to reverse through a small gap in a narrow street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People carrier' looks like a family car; 'to reverse' makes EROP, and 'in' sets it inside A LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane carries passengers, so it is a people carrier in a literal sense.
